I'm writing the warn hook now. It's a small script in futon3c, plus one entry in your user settings, and I'll pipe-test it before wiring it in.Now I'll prove it fires in this session. I'm a pouch, so this is a live test:It fired, and the command still ran. Now I'm committing the script and updating the backlog entry:㊢ ("have a look at the recent claude-11 record") claude-11 shows exactly the failure this hook is for. Its Lean session servers (the warm `Init` server and the first Mathlib import) were started with `run_in_background`. Both died when its pouch was torn down between turns. It first told you they hit "a 30-minute timeout". After your correction it switched to bg.py and wrote a memory note, which adds one thing I hadn't covered: **Monitor** watches die with the pouch too.

㊢ (done) The warn hook is in and working:
- **Script:** `futon3c/scripts/claude-hooks/bg_warn.py` (futon3c `66da03c9`).
- **Wiring:** `~/.claude/settings.json`, PreToolUse on `Bash|Monitor`. The old file is kept as `settings.json.bak-2026-10-10`.
- **Who it warns:** only pouch agents, meaning `FUTON_AGENT_ID` is set, so terminal sessions are left alone.
- **What it catches:** `run_in_background`, `nohup`/`setsid`/`disown`, a trailing `&`, and any Monitor call.
- **How it warns:** the agent gets a note telling it to use `bg.py launch "<cmd>" --agent <id>`, with "if it finishes within this turn, ignore this" for short jobs. It never blocks a command.

㊬ (checked) The pipe test covered 8 cases. `2>&1`, `&&`, commands that already use bg.py, and sessions without an agent id all stay silent. I also proved it live in this session: my own `sleep 0.1 &` produced the warning in my context, and the command still ran. The backlog entry in §5 is now marked **adopted** (futon0 `e661585`).

㊟ (scope) Other pouches pick it up the next time they load settings. Any pouch that's warm right now may need a fresh turn or a restart first. If the warning turns out to be too soft, the next step would be to deny `run_in_background` alone and keep warning on the rest.

previous_reply_acts.label: "surely there must be a "tool" or "skill" or MCP"
previous_reply_acts.text:
🈖 ("surely there must be a "tool" or "skill" or MCP") There is, and for this case the strongest of them is a **hook**, not a skill or an MCP tool. The four options, strongest first:
1. **Hook.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook on Bash sees every command before it runs. It can deny anything that sets `run_in_background` or uses `nohup`, `setsid` or a trailing `&`, and reply "use `scripts/bg.py launch "<cmd>" --agent <id>`". It runs every time, so it doesn't depend on the model remembering anything.
2. **Skill.** It loads when its description matches the task, but the model still has to pick it.
3. **MCP or native `bg_launch` tool.** It makes the right action easy, but nothing stops a bare `&`.
4. **Prose in CLAUDE.md.** That's where the rule lives now, and it's why you keep reminding agents.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.label: "I've rolled my own REPL is the only thing to "blame""
previous_reply_acts.text: ㊟ ("I've rolled my own REPL is the only thing to "blame"") Mostly not. Any rule kept in prose fails this way, with or without a custom REPL. And your REPL doesn't block the standard fix. Agency's pouches run `claude --print` with no `--setting-sources` restriction (I checked `agent_pouch.clj`), so a hook in your user settings should apply to every claude-N. Hooks can deny a command even under `bypassPermissions`. Before relying on it, I'd confirm on one pouch that it actually fires.
